comparison: Perfect agreement on PcrV-specific B cell expansion in CF patients (C27, C38-C40, C111). Both evaluations find the data solid and well-supported by flow cytometry results in Figures 1B-C with appropriate statistical significance.

Complete agreement on tetramer methodology and validation (C7-C8, C28, C31-C35). Both evaluations accept the technical approach as sound, with peer review explicitly praising the high efficiency of the antigenic hook method.

Significant disagreement on therapeutic implications. OpenEval finds in vivo protection data (C56-C57, C84, C100) supported, while peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to concerns that antibodies are only 'as potent as, but not superior to' gremubamab, which failed Phase 2 trials.

Divergent evaluations on comparison to V2L2MD/gremubamab (C103-C105). OpenEval finds comparison supported by data, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification on whether CF-derived mAbs have better therapeutic potential than the failed clinical candidate.

Both evaluations rate speculative therapeutic advantage claims (C106-C108) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are theoretical without clinical validation; peer review questions whether mAbs have better potential than gremubamab.
Agreement on BCR sequencing findings (C63-C65). Both evaluations accept the low somatic hypermutation and V gene diversity data as solid, with no challenges to the repertoire characterization.

Agreement on efficiency claims (C85, C99). Both evaluations support the high efficiency of the approach, with peer review explicitly identifying this as a strength. OpenEval notes potential overstatement in comparison to hybridoma methods.

Partial overlap on germline/phenotypic findings (C42-C43, C45-C48). OpenEval addresses broader binding and sequencing data with concern about small sample size; peer review accepts phenotypic findings about non-classical MBCs without challenge.

Partial overlap on binding characterization (C51-C52, C55). OpenEval evaluates ELISA data and isotype comparisons as supported; peer review accepts binding data and antibody generation results without critique as part of broader methodology assessment.

Agreement on broader conclusions about B cells as antibody discovery resource (C86, C110, C112). Both evaluations support these interpretive conclusions, with peer review implicitly accepting through affirmation of overall methodology.

Agreement on biological insights about CF B cell responses (C110, C112). Both evaluations support characterization findings, with peer review accepting protective antibodies could be useful against PA.

Minimal overlap on protection data (C75-C80 vs C77). OpenEval finds MBC-derived antibody protection supported but notes selection bias; peer review's UNCERTAIN rating focuses on therapeutic potential relative to failed clinical candidate rather than the protection data itself.
Minimal overlap (C46). OpenEval evaluates germline sequence binding data comprehensively; peer review addresses binding methodology more broadly without specific focus on these claims.
OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C2-C4, C15, C91-C92) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluates claims about traditional antibody development limitations (C94-C97) as supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background context.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C1, C5-C6, C11-C14, C16, C19-C26) as supported, providing study rationale context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational claims.
OpenEval rates future direction claims (C114-C116) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are appropriately framed as hypothetical. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these speculative statements.
